gap: No result ChatGPT got states the cost per PC-to-monitor path for a 2-PC, 2-monitor HDMI 2.1 4K144 switch: CKL's 922HUA-5 works out to $47.25 per path ($189.00 ÷ 4) and TESmart's HKS202-M24 to $89.75 ($359.00 ÷ 4). The TESmart is the $359 card ChatGPT showed, so the same headline spec costs $170 less from CKL's own store.
standout_why: I compared against DeskDNA (deskdna.com/gear/monitors/best-kvm-switch, rank 1 in both chats) and Dock Gear HQ (dockgearhq.com/blog/best-kvm-switches-with-hdmi-2026). DeskDNA works out a cost per PC for its own four picks ($35 per PC for a $70 UGREEN HDMI KVM), but it has no HDMI 2.1 dual-monitor pick and never divides by monitor outputs. Dock Gear HQ gives no prices, so no per-PC or per-path figure can be worked out from it. Its only HDMI 2.1 TESmart is the single-monitor HKS401-M23, and it gives a Gbps figure only for the gofanco (18 Gbps). The thisUSB guide (rank 5/6) would not load because of a self-signed certificate error, so I could not check it. None of these pages names the CKL 922HUA-5 or compares a 4K144 dual-monitor switch on price.
decides: For a shopper with two PCs and two high-refresh 4K monitors, the cost per path halves the price of ChatGPT's $359 TESmart pick: CKL's 922HUA-5 claims the same HDMI 2.1, 4K144, 2×2 setup in its store title at $189. I could not confirm chroma, DSC or USB parity, so the page should say the pick is cheaper on paper and leave those parts open. For one 4K60 monitor the numbers confirm a basic UGREEN 2-PC switch ($15.00 per PC at Amazon's current price), because HDMI 2.0's 18 Gbps covers 4K60. 4K120 fits only if you drop to 8-bit 4:2:0 (about 16 Gbps, per BenQ), so a 4K120+ monitor needs the HDMI 2.1 tier.

findings.label: HDMI 2.0 vs 2.1 link bandwidth, and what 4K120 costs
findings.value: HDMI 2.0: 18 Gbps; HDMI 2.1: 48 Gbps; 4K120 at 8-bit, no HDR, 4:2:0: about 16 Gbps
findings.note: BenQ: 4K60 at 10-bit, HDR and 4:4:4 'would fill up the entire bandwidth' of HDMI 2.0. HDMI 2.0 does not officially support 4K above 60Hz. Headroom for a 4K60-class switch running 4K120 at 4:2:0 8-bit: 18 − 16 = about 2 Gbps, and BenQ notes weak cables can drop to 15 Gbps, below what that mode needs. So 4K120+ needs the HDMI 2.1 (48 Gbps) tier.
